question: What is the main purpose of the systemic circulation?

options.A: Filter waste products in the kidneys
options.B: Remove carbon dioxide from the lungs
options.C: Warm up blood before it reaches the brain
options.D: Deliver oxygenated blood to body tissues

explanation: The systemic circuit is responsible for pumping oxygen and nutrients out to all body organs and tissues. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T12#GNS111_U2_T12_h1)

question: Why does the systemic circulation require higher pressure than the pulmonary circulation?

options.A: It has to travel a much longer distance through the whole body
options.B: It must push blood upward against gravity at all times
options.C: It connects directly to the high-pressure kidney filters
options.D: It handles both oxygen and carbon dioxide simultaneously

explanation: Because systemic blood must reach distant organs from head to toe, the left side of the heart generates much higher pressure than the right side. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T12#GNS111_U2_T12_h1)

question: Which heart chamber pumps oxygenated blood directly into the aorta?
explanation: The left ventricle is the thick-walled muscular chamber that forcefully ejects blood into the aorta. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T12#GNS111_U2_T12_h2)

question: What is the function of the coronary arteries that branch off the ascending aorta?

options.A: Carry blood to the upper brain and scalp
options.B: Drain waste products from the lungs
options.C: Connect the aorta to the pulmonary trunk
options.D: Supply oxygen directly to the heart muscle

explanation: The coronary arteries branch off right at the base of the aorta to feed the hardworking muscle tissue of the heart. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T12#GNS111_U2_T12_h2)

question: Which blood vessels act as control valves to regulate blood flow into local tissues?
explanation: Arterioles have muscular walls that contract or relax to control the volume of blood entering capillary beds. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T12#GNS111_U2_T12_h3)

question: What happens to the arterioles in your muscles when you start heavy exercise?

options.A: They collapse completely to stop bleeding
options.B: They harden permanently to boost pressure
options.C: They dilate to let more blood through
options.D: They constrict to block fast blood flow

explanation: Working muscles need more oxygen, so local arterioles relax and open wide to increase blood supply. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T12#GNS111_U2_T12_h3)

question: What physical feature of capillaries makes the exchange of substances possible?

options.A: Walls that are only one cell thick
options.C: Valves that stop blood from flowing backward
options.D: Thick muscular layers that pulse strongly

explanation: The ultra-thin single-cell wall of a capillary allows easy diffusion of gases and nutrients between blood and tissue cells. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T12#GNS111_U2_T12_h4)

question: How do oxygen and glucose generally move from the capillary blood into the body tissues?

options.B: Active pumping by white blood cells

explanation: Substances move naturally from an area of higher concentration in the blood to an area of lower concentration in the tissues via diffusion. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T12#GNS111_U2_T12_h4)

question: What is the function of the one-way valves inside medium veins?

options.A: Filter bacteria out of returning blood
options.B: Add oxygen back into venous blood

explanation: Venous valves ensure that blood moves in only one direction—toward the heart—against the pull of gravity. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T12#GNS111_U2_T12_h5)

question: A patient sits still in a chair for many hours on a long flight. Which mechanism for venous return is temporarily reduced?
explanation: Without leg movement, the skeletal muscle pump cannot help push venous blood upward, which can lead to pooling. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T12#GNS111_U2_T12_h5)

question: What does peripheral resistance refer to in the circulatory system?

options.B: Friction of blood against vessel walls
options.C: The pumping strength of the left atrium
options.D: The speed of oxygen binding to hemoglobin

explanation: Peripheral resistance is the drag or friction blood experiences as it travels through the blood vessels. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T12#GNS111_U2_T12_h6)

question: What happens to blood pressure if small arterioles constrict and become narrower?

options.B: Blood pressure fluctuates wildly every second

explanation: Narrowing the blood vessels increases resistance, which raises the pressure needed to push blood through them. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T12#GNS111_U2_T12_h6)

question: Which assessment finding is a reliable indicator of poor peripheral tissue perfusion?
explanation: Cold, pale, or cyanotic skin often means blood flow to the skin and outer tissues is reduced. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T12#GNS111_U2_T12_h7)

question: Why is the patient's level of consciousness checked when assessing systemic circulation?

options.A: Alertness proves that heart valves are closing correctly
options.B: Consciousness measures how much glucose is stored in the liver
options.C: Mental status directly controls blood vessel width in the legs
options.D: The brain is very sensitive to drops in blood flow and oxygen

explanation: The brain requires a constant supply of oxygenated blood, making confusion or sleepiness an early warning sign of poor perfusion. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T12#GNS111_U2_T12_h7)

question: What term describes tissue damage caused by a lack of adequate blood supply?
explanation: Ischemia is the medical term for inadequate blood flow to a tissue or organ, depriving it of needed oxygen. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T12#GNS111_U2_T12_h8)

question: Which of the following is a common sign of chronic poor systemic circulation in the lower extremities?

options.A: Excessive sweating on the soles of feet
options.B: Sudden swelling with a hot red surface
options.C: Slow-healing sores or ulcers on the feet
options.D: Inability to move the toes at all

explanation: Poor blood flow means tissues lack the nutrients and oxygen needed to repair minor cuts, leading to slow-healing wounds. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T12#GNS111_U2_T12_h8)
